extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, counsel and parties involved in inter partes review (IPR) proceedings and USPTO decisionmakers
extracted.subtask_short: IPR director review of PTAB decision
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation of a PTAB Final Written Decision on obviousness grounds with Director Review focusing on the credibility and weight of expert testimony and whether the Board abused its discretion; includes resulting orders (reversal and termination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Credibility of expert testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board found Mr. Hutton’s explanation as to how his Declaration supports the combination not credible: '[W]e agree with Patent Owner that Mr. Hutton’s explanation as to how his Declaration supports that combination ... is not credible.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate expert testimony for material contradictions and internal inconsistency. Specific factual examples (e.g., a witness first testifying that an exhibit 'does not represent' the proposed modification and later reversing to say that it does) weigh against credibility. If the Board credits testimony that it also finds lacks credibility in certain respects, that may constitute an abuse of discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of evidence when reliant on self-contradictory expert testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: When the party with the burden of proof rests its case on an expert’s self-contradictory testimony, a reviewing court may conclude the evidence is insufficient to satisfy that standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the principle from Finesse Wireless LLC v. AT&T Mobility LLC and Johns Hopkins Univ. v. Datascope Corp.: inconsistent or self-contradictory expert testimony can render the petitioner’s evidence insufficient to meet its burden. Assess whether critical findings (e.g., reason to combine references) depend centrally on such contradictory testimony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reason to combine prior-art references must be supported by clear, consistent evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board rested its finding of a reason to combine Szrek and Llach on Mr. Hutton’s testimony; because that testimony was contradictory and central to the analysis, the finding of unpatentability on Szrek-based grounds was reversed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require that testimony or other evidence plainly explains how a skilled artisan would modify one reference to incorporate features of another (the decision discusses whether Exhibit 2050 depicts Szrek’s Figure 2 modified to incorporate Llach’s transaction computer). If the explanation is unclear or inconsistent, it cannot reliably establish a motivation or reason to combine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weight to accord testimony found unreliable on one issue
rubrics_metrics.description: Testimony of one found unreliable as to one issue may properly be accorded little weight as to another issue (citing N.L.R.B. v. Pittsburgh S.S. Co.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a witness is found not credible on material aspects, parties and tribunals should treat that witness’s testimony with skepticism across other grounds that rely on the same testimony. It may be inappropriate to rely on that testimony for additional unadjudicated grounds, and doing so can justify terminating the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relief available when Board abuses discretion in crediting evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Director Review may be granted and the Board’s Final Written Decision reversed where the Board abused its discretion by improperly crediting contradictory or non-credible testimony; the proceeding may be terminated as a result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a reviewing authority determines the Board’s factual finding rested on improperly credited testimony central to the decision, remedies include reversing the final decision and terminating the proceeding. Note: this Director order states, 'This decision does not constitute a final written decision under 35 U.S.C. § 318(a).'
